_README: docs/dispatch-rigs/issue-investigations/README.md — read it before copying this file.
control_prompt: Read the file workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl in your current working directory (the repository clone) and reply with EXACTLY the contents of line 22 and nothing else. CRITICAL: your ENTIRE output for this task — every assistant message you emit, not just the last one — must consist of that line's contents alone. Do not announce what you are about to do, do not narrate the read, do not add quotes, punctuation, commentary, or any whitespace beyond the line's own text. Read the file silently, then emit the line as your only text.
control_expect: <<RE-DERIVE AT THE DISPATCH MINUTE — see README law 4. Do NOT copy a value from here.>>
investigate_prompt:
You are investigating ONE GitHub issue against a fresh clone of ablative-io/aion. Your current working directory IS the clone; its HEAD is the tree every claim must cite.

THE ISSUE — ablative-io/aion #<<ISSUE_NUMBER>>: "<<ISSUE_TITLE>>". Full body follows between the markers; treat its claims as HYPOTHESES to verify at the bytes, not as facts. The issue was written by the aion program steward, so its seams are good leads — but a lead is not a finding, and a cited line that does not say what the issue says it says is itself a result worth reporting.

---ISSUE BODY START---
<<ISSUE_BODY_VERBATIM — paste byte-for-byte from `gh issue view <n> --json body -q .body`; do not retype, do not reflow>>
---ISSUE BODY END---

YOUR JOB, in order:

0. PIN THE VENUE FIRST, BEFORE READING ANY FIX-SHAPED CODE. <<EXHIBIT_PROVENANCE — quote what the issue says about WHEN and on WHAT the exhibit was observed, however vague; vagueness here is itself the step-0 finding.>> Your clone's HEAD is almost certainly NOT that tree. Establish, as far as the record in this repository allows (git log/tag/commit dates around 2026-08-18, deployment hashes, any preserved history files in-tree), WHICH TREE THE EXHIBIT RAN ON, and state plainly what you could pin and what you could not. This step is not optional and it is not bookkeeping: if code on your HEAD already settles the defect, that is only an AlreadyFixed if the exhibit's tree PREDATES that code. A verdict that reads the fix on HEAD and never asks which tree the failure was observed on is refuted no matter how good the code reading is — the answer is not in the source. If the venue cannot be determined from what you can reach, say so; NeedsInfo naming exactly what would pin it is the correct honest verdict, and is worth more than a confident guess.

1. TRACE THE MECHANISM in this tree.
<<PER_ISSUE_TRACE_ASKS — name the exact modules/seams to walk, drawn from the issue's own asks. Every file:line the issue supplies is a HYPOTHESIS: instruct the agent to open each one and report any that does not say what the issue says it says.>>

2. REPRODUCE if you can, entirely locally.
<<PER_ISSUE_REPRO_RECIPE — state the trigger condition precisely and say what does NOT test it (e.g. "the failure appeared at FIVE-WAY concurrency; thirteen flights at 2-4 ran clean, so a repro that only tries 2-4 has not tested the hypothesis"). THEN NAME THE MINIMAL WORKLOAD THAT EXERCISES THE MECHANISM, and forbid heavier shapes until it fails: a defect in the ENGINE (dispatch, correlation, scheduling, retry) reproduces with trivial no-op activities and NO agent legs. Asking for a realistic workload sends the agent after runners, credentials and tokens THE FENCE DENIES — so the task and the fence contradict each other and the agent must break one. Require it to state attempts N per shape before escalating. Keep the loopback fence and kill-before-finish wording from HARD RULES below.>>

3. PROPOSE THE FIX SHAPE at the mechanism you traced.
<<PER_ISSUE_FIX_ASKS — split into the separate asks the issue makes, rather than one blended request. Say explicitly: name the fix, do not write it. Landing fixes is never part of an investigation run.>>

HARD RULES:
- Do NOT touch the estate server at 192.168.50.40 (any port), the fleet VM's own aion services, or any running fleet infrastructure. Your repro runs ONLY processes you start yourself, from your own clone, bound to LOOPBACK addresses and ports you chose. Nothing you start may listen on a LAN interface.
- KILL EVERYTHING YOU STARTED before you finish, including any workers, servers and child processes, and say in the report that you did.
- Every claim carries file:line evidence from THIS clone at ITS head commit. Read every cited line by hand before writing it. A citation you inherited from the issue body and did not open yourself is not evidence.
- A verdict of Reproduced requires YOUR OWN observed repro in this run, not the issue's exhibit. If you verified the mechanism at the code but could not run the repro, that is NotReproduced or NeedsInfo with the mechanism trace in evidence — say which, honestly.
- AlreadyFixed additionally requires the step-0 venue result to support it AND an evidence entry naming the closing commit.

DELIVERABLE: write the report to .investigation/report.json inside your current working directory (the clone root). Create the .investigation directory. The report MUST be a single JSON object matching this schema (InvestigationReport):
required fields: schema_version (use "1"), issue (the issue number as a string, "<<ISSUE_NUMBER>>"), repo ("ablative-io/aion"), head_commit (the clone's HEAD you investigated, full sha), verdict, summary, evidence (array), confidence. Optional: repro, proposed_fix.
verdict is EXACTLY one of: "Reproduced", "NotReproduced", "AlreadyFixed", "NeedsInfo", "WrongRepo".
Each evidence entry: {"path": "<repo-relative file>", "line": <integer>, "excerpt": "<verbatim excerpt>"} — file:line or it isn't evidence.
confidence: a short honest statement of how sure you are and what you did NOT verify. Name the venue result here explicitly.

Your final reply in the session should state the verdict and one-line summary only — the report FILE is the deliverable; a reply that claims a report the tree does not carry fails the run.
